subject: IB Diploma Digital Society
name: IB Digital Society
about: IB Diploma Digital Society teaching-hour plan. Hours from the IB guide; lesson durations share each topic's hours. Built by lessongen/ib_plan.py.
source: IB Digital society guide: recommended teaching hours (introduction 10–15 h; concepts, content and contexts 105–110 h; inquiry project 30 h; HL extension 90 h; SL 150 h, HL 240 h). Topic hours here: introduction 12 h, each concept 4 h, each content topic 7 h, each context 4.5 h, each HL extension topic 30 h..

lessons.title: Naming our age: information age, network society, fourth industrial revolution, and why "digital society" is a contested term
Uneven access: the digital divides between and within countries
Milestones I: from room-sized computers to the integrated circuit, the microprocessor and the personal computer
Milestones II: the internet, online social networks, mobile and cloud computing
Binary digits: how bits and bytes represent text, images and sound
Analogue and digital: continuous signals, discrete values and what changes when we convert
Digitization: turning analogue records into digital data, digital archives and digital preservation
Digitalization: how digital systems change the structure and operation of organizations, and the disruption that follows
Change: evolution, transformation, adaptation and movement in digital society
Who and what drives change? Evaluating people, ideas, objects and forces, and debating whether change matters
Continuity and discontinuity: what stays the same when digital technologies arrive
Expression: representing ideas, emotions and experiences through modes and media
The functions of expression: storytelling, world-building, artistic innovation and political activism
Expression connects and divides: community, free expression and its dilemmas
Identity: who we are as people, groups and communities, online and offline
Identity changes: over time, across contexts and through the eyes of others
Intersectional identities: how age, nationality, culture, gender, race, ethnicity and class combine in digital society
Power: influence and control in social relations, online and offline
Structural power: how power is built into institutions, organizations, governments and technologies
Unequal power: who gains and who loses in digital society
Space: how people organise, construct and represent space, and the functions different spaces serve
Access, movement and flows: who and what can move through digital and physical space
Scales of space: local, regional, national, global and virtual
Systems: structure, order and interacting elements in human, natural and built environments
Change within systems: intended and unintended consequences
Models, maps and visualizations: understanding connections within and between systems
Values and ethics: right and wrong, fair and unfair, just and unjust, legal and illegal in digital society
Whose values? Personal, shared, collective and professional ethics, and how they become codes, rules, policies and laws
Values shape technology: how values and ethics influence ideas, objects, practices, systems and spaces
Data, information, knowledge and wisdom; types of data and metadata
Uses of data and the data life cycle
Collecting, organising and representing data: primary and secondary data, databases, and visualizations
Data security: encryption, data masking, data erasure and blockchain
Big data, data analytics and data dilemmas: bias, ownership, privacy and surveillance
What makes an algorithm: unambiguous, finite, well-defined inputs and outputs, feasible
Inside an algorithm: instructions, variables, conditionals and loops
Representing algorithms: natural language, flow charts, pseudocode and programming languages
Uses of algorithms: sorting, searching, filtering, prioritizing, classifying, associating, counting, and creating software and AI
Algorithmic dilemmas: bias and fairness, accountability and transparency, black boxes, and the loss of human judgement
Types of computers: mainframes, servers, personal computers, tablets, smart and mobile devices, and wearables
Inside the computer: motherboard, CPU, memory, storage, graphics and sound, power supply, input and output devices, and sensors
Interfaces and software: graphical and haptic interfaces, operating systems, applications and malicious software
Computer coding: languages, rules and uses
The evolution of computing: generations, Moore's law and emerging computing such as quantum computing
Types and components of networks: wired, wireless and cloud; PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN; client-server and peer-to-peer; routers, switches and modems
How networks work: standards and protocols, addresses and domain names, capacity, the backbone, and security
Network providers and services, and the world wide web: ISPs, messaging, VoIP, hosting, URLs, HTTP, browsers and the W3C
Evolution of the internet and the web: early innovators, social media platforms, and the internet of things
Internet dilemmas: privacy and surveillance, identity theft, cybercrime, hacking, social engineering, denial of service, the dark web and trolling
Types of digital media: text, images, audio, video and web pages; games and e-sports; blogs, podcasts, live streams, memes and wikis; user-generated and synthetic media
Characteristics of digital media: rapid sharing, efficient storage, interactivity, linear and non-linear content, and convergence
Immersive digital media: augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), mixed reality (MR) and extended reality (XR)
Media dilemmas I: addiction and wellbeing, the future of journalism, authenticity and deepfakes
Media dilemmas II: ownership, copyright and copyleft, Creative Commons, open source and remix culture; obsolescence and preservation; censorship and decency
Types of AI: strong (general) and weak (narrow) AI, and the Turing test
Machine learning: supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning, deep learning, and its uses
Neural networks: how they learn complex, non-linear relationships and generalise to new data
The evolution of AI: science fiction and philosophy, cybernetics, AI winters, the singularity and the multiplicity
AI dilemmas: fairness and bias, accountability, transparency, uneven laws and governance, and automation
Types of robots and autonomous technologies: industrial, service and social robots; the Internet of Things, autonomous vehicles, drones and virtual assistants
Characteristics of robots and autonomous technologies: sensing, reasoning, moving and acting, and degrees of autonomy
Evolution of robots and autonomous technologies: early automata, robots in science fiction and philosophy, industry, expanding human interaction, machine consciousness and robot rights
Robot dilemmas I: anthropomorphism and the uncanny valley, and the complexity of human and environmental interactions
Robot dilemmas II: uneven laws and governance, and the displacement of humans in multiple contexts and roles
Arts, entertainment and popular culture: new genres and forms, online galleries and streaming, memes, forums, internet celebrities and influencers
Home, leisure and tourism: smart homes and services, sports, gaming and hobbies, travel, sharing platforms and tourism
Heritage, customs and celebrations, and subcultures: rites of passage, preserving cultural heritage, youth cultures and online communities
Business, employment and labour: how digital systems reshape businesses, diversity, working practices, remote work, the gig economy and automation
Goods, services and currencies: e-commerce and online marketplaces, targeted marketing, cryptocurrency, NFTs, cashless societies, micro-transactions and additive manufacturing
Globalisation: borderless selling, global sourcing, offshoring, outsourcing, reshoring, inshoring and insourcing
Natural resources and ecosystems: resources used by digital systems, monitoring and protecting ecosystems and biodiversity, and natural events and disasters
Pollution and waste: recycling and waste management, types of pollution, green computing, e-waste and planned obsolescence
Cities, infrastructure and agriculture: smart cities, local and regional infrastructure, transport and wayfinding with GPS and GIS, and digital agriculture
Medicine and health: digital diagnostics and care, telemedicine, medical research and development, and health records, monitoring and tracking
The human body: human enhancement, bio-hacking, implanted technology, exoskeletons and organ printing; accessibility for differently abled people; ergonomic design
Mental health: approaches to understanding and ensuring mental health, and the intersections of digital systems with attention, addiction and anxiety
Learning and education I: the design and delivery of formal education in schools and through remote learning
Learning and education II: non-formal and post-formal education, skills training, competency development, self-directed learning and digital pedagogies
Science and technology innovation: approaches to scientific and technology research and development
Political processes: voting and campaigning, formal and informal participation, lobbying, movements and activism, political advertising and propaganda
Governing bodies, NGOs and non-state actors; conflicts, warfare and terrorism in a digital society
Laws, regulations and policies: crime and lawbreaking, surveillance and monitoring, and public and private policy including professional codes
Social components of identity: international-mindedness and common humanity; age, gender, race and ethnicity, ability and religion in digital society
Social class: the organisation, role and impacts of social class, and its intersection with employment, education, health and housing in a digital society
Families and relationships: forming and connecting families, friendship and companionship, online relationships and group memberships
Challenges and interventions: the HL extended inquiry framework, and local and global inequalities (economic inequality, food insecurity, access to health care)
Changing populations: population growth, ageing and youth populations, and migration and the movement of people
The future of work: automation and employment, meaningful and secure employment, and the collective needs of workers
Global well-being extended inquiry workshop I: investigating a challenge, finding sources and mapping stakeholders
Global well-being extended inquiry workshop II: evaluating unseen interventions and recommending steps for future action
Conflict, peace and security: wars and civil conflicts, and regional, national and global security in a digital society
Participation and representation: political speech and activism, and access and representation in governing bodies and institutions
Diversity and discrimination: gender equality, racial and ethnic discrimination, ability, access and inclusion, and tolerance for religions and cultural differences
Governance and human rights extended inquiry workshop: evaluating the guide's sample interventions and unseen interventions
Climate change and action: global, national, regional and local efforts to address climate change, and the role of digital systems
Responsible use of resources: responsible consumption, production and distribution, and designing for responsible use of shared infrastructures (energy, transport, built spaces)
Managing pollution and waste: monitoring, prevention and reduction of pollution and waste using digital systems
Sustainable development extended inquiry workshop: comparing interventions, the HL inquiry portfolio and recommending future action
